sentences.text:
This application coming on for admission this day, the  following:
 ORDER
This petition has been preferred by the petitioner for extension of time of temporary bail granted to her by order dated 13.10.2023 in M.Cr.C. No.14506/2023.

In the alternate a prayer has also been made for granting regular bail to the petitioner.
02.

The petitioner is implicated in connection with Crime No.225/2022 registered at Police Station City Kotwali, District Mandsaur (M.P) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 380, 328 and 120-B of IPC.
The petitioner is in custody since 29.04.2022.

sentences.text: According to the prosecution, on 16-04-2022, the complainant Shyamlal made a written report to the police that he was in search of a girl for marriage of his son Praveen, he had met co-accused Mangla, who suggested the applicant Aarti for the said marriage.
The complainant agreed for the same.
On 16-04-2022 co-accused Mangla alongwith Arjun Prajapati, Aarti and one Puja came on a four wheeler from Bhopal to his house.
The complainant stated that they shall perform the marriage through Arya Samaj.
Mangla stated that she shall search the mother and relative of the applicant after two days for performance of marriage and till then Aarti may stay in his house.
The complainant agreed to the same.
Thereupon applicant stayed in his house and the complainant made over a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- to Arjun by way of commission for arranging the marriage.

On 18-04-2022 at about 4:00 pm, when complainant had gone to the market living behind his wife Vishnubai, his elder daughter-in-law Priyanka and his elder son Sandeep and Aarti in the house and after one hour when he came back he saw his wife Vishnuabi and elder daughter-in-law un-concisous and applicant missing.
He then called his son Sandeep who came over and took Vishnubai and Priyanka to the hospital.
After coming back they searched the house and found that Rs.1,00,000/- cash kept for marriage of Praveen and certain gold jewellery missing from the house.

His son Sandeep informed him that the applicant had made tea but he did not consume the same,
whereas his mother and wife Priyanaka consumed it.
He had gone to his house after having food.
The applicant had mixed some poisonous substance in the tea as a result of which Vishnubai and Sandeep became unconscious and she ran away with the aforesaid items.
On the basis of the allegations, the applicant has been implicated and arrested for the present offence.
04. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that she is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
A document as regards marriage between her and the son of the complainant
has already been executed.

On 8- 04-2022 her in-laws had beaten her hence she had gone to the police station to report the said incident but the police did not register her report hence she came back to her house at Hoshangabad and lodged a report against her in-laws and also filed an application under Section 125 of Cr.PC for grant of maintenance against them.
It is only for the purpose of saving themselves that the complainant and his family members have lodged false complaint against her.
No recovery has been made from her and she has not received any amount from the complainant.
The medical report also does not support the prosecution case.
It is further submitted that despite lapse of a period of almost two years not a single witness has been examined before the trial Court.
The applicant has been appearing before the trial Court on each and every date of hearing.
One of the co-accused is absconding and the matter is still pending before the trial Court for his appearance.
All the other co
-accused in the matter have already been enlarged on bail by various orders passed in various bail applications.
It is hence submitted that applicant be granted permanent bail.

05. The prayer has been opposed by the learned counsel for the respondent/State submitting that in view of the allegations levelled against the applicant, she is not entitled to be released on bail merely on the basis of her custody period.
06. The applicant has been in custody since the date of her arrest on 29.04.2022 subject to the period for which she has been released on bail.

sentences.text: Almost a period of two years has elapsed since then.
Not a single witness has been examined before the trial Court as of yet hence it is apparent that the trial shall take a long time for its conclusion.
One of the co-accused is still absconding.
The applicant is a lady and has recently given birth to a child, who is presently aged about 14 months.
The child would be required to be looked after by the applicant and the upbringing of the child in custody would not be desirable.
All the other co-accused have already been enlarged on regular bail by this Court by different orders passed in different bail applications.
Thus looking to the fact of pendency of the proceedings and of the applicant giving birth to a child, I deem it fit to enlarge her on regular bail.

07. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail subject to her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the Court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
08. Present M.Cr.C. is accordingly allowed and disposed off.

(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE Shilpa Smt. Aarti Vind vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45926812/
